items.text: In a regional public health agency, does validating syndromic surveillance alerts with a structured checklist, compared with usual validation, on randomly allocated duty days over six months, shorten the time from alert to validation decision without increasing true events dismissed at the first alert?
items.population: Syndromic surveillance alerts generated on duty days from January to June 2027
items.intervention: Structured validation checklist with an escalation rule
items.comparator: Usual unwritten validation by the epidemiologist on duty
items.outcome: Time from alert to validation decision; true events dismissed at first alert as the balancing outcome
items.setting: Regional public health agency, six duty epidemiologists

finer: Feasible with existing logs and staff; interesting to the director and other agencies; novel in using day-level randomisation; ethical as program evaluation; relevant to whether the checklist becomes standard.
summary: One PICOT question with a balancing outcome for missed events.
